question: How many atoms of hydrogen are there in Ammonium Chloride?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Four.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Ammonium chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula **NH₄Cl **and a **white crystalline salt **that is highly soluble in water.
 
• There are 4 atoms of **Hydrogen**, one nitrogen, and one chloride atom. 
 
• In its naturally occurring mineralogic form, it is known as **sal ammoniac**.
 
• Ammonium Chloride gives an acidic solution by dissolving in water.
 
• It vaporizes without melting at 340 °C (644 °F) to form equal volumes of ammonia and hydrogen chloride.
